jobs.title: Analytical Chemist
jobs.description:
At Pattern Bioscience, we're tackling antibiotic resistance, one of the biggest public health challenges of our time. We use machine learning and microfluidics to quickly recognize the bacteria causing an infection and to predict which drugs will cure the infection.

We are hiring an Analytical Chemist to join our Consumable Manufacturing team during a critical inflection point in our company journey. We are actively investing in scaling our consumable production while developing the next assays for our platform. Your work will be key in ensuring precision in and quality of our reagent formulations for both current and future assays. Through your work, you will have the opportunity to work with research and process scientists, reagent manufacturing associates, and quality and automation engineers.

#### **Three Month Goals**

* Support development and validation of analytical methods for new assay panel research and development
* Independently manage routine HPLC qualification of manufacturing materials
* Independently manage inventory of reference materials and check standards to support HPLC program

#### **How You Will Contribute**

* Develop, optimize, and validate HPLC methods used for raw material, in-process, and finished reagent testing.
* Perform routine and non-routine HPLC and other analytical instrumentation testing (pH, conductivity, UV-Vis, refractometry, FTIR, NMR etc) to support batch release, stability studies, and process/manufacturing support.
* Following released procedures, formulate analytical standards for use in HPLC analysis.
* Troubleshoot chromatographic and instrument issues (columns, mobile phases, detectors, autosamplers, pumps) to minimize downtime and maintain lab operations.
* Author, review, and revise analytical test methods, SOPs, and work instructions; support the creation and execution of method validation protocols and reports.
* Support method transfer, method development, and equipment/test method validation activities for new and existing products.
* Analyze and interpret analytical data, including trending and statistical process control (SPC), to monitor equipment, method, and process performance over time.
* Investigate out-of-specification (OOS) and out-of-trend (OOT) results and atypical events; support nonconformance root cause analysis and CAPAs.
* Maintain, calibrate, and qualify analytical equipment systems and associated laboratory instrumentation; coordinate preventive maintenance and service with vendors.
* Partner with R&D, Manufacturing, and Quality teams to define material specifications, test methods, and acceptance criteria for reagents and raw materials.
* Maintain compliance with Good Documentation Practices, data integrity principles, and 21 CFR Part 11 requirements for all laboratory records and electronic data.
* Provide training and oversight to laboratory personnel on analytical methods, instrument operation, and data review.
* Support internal and external audits and regulatory inspections related to analytical testing.
* Are a thorough and relentless problem-solver, pursuing issues to their root cause.
* Keep the big picture in mind, knowing what needs to happen today to enable projects for later in the week, engaging subject matter experts or other teams as needed.
* Stay calm, adaptable, and flexible under changing priorities and the introduction of new methods.
* Excel in data analysis, particularly for chromatography data.
* Communicate clearly and efficiently in both oral and written formats, including technical writing and GxP documentation.

#### **Desired Education and Experience**

* B.S. in Chemistry, Biochemistry, Chemical Engineering, or a related scientific field.
* Min 2 years of hands-on HPLC and/or analytical chemistry laboratory experience, preferably within a regulated (GxP, FDA, or ISO 13485) environment.
* Demonstrated hands-on experience in analytical method development, qualification, validation, routine operation and troubleshooting.
* Working knowledge of complementary analytical techniques (e.g., UV-Vis/spectrophotometry, NMR, FTIR) is a plus.
* A strong understanding of FDA regulations and ISO 13485 requirements for IVD medical device development and production.
* Proficiency with chromatography data systems (e.g., Empower, Chromeleon, or similar CDS software).
* Understanding of cleanroom operations, BSL2 protocols, Good Documentation Practice, and GxP data integrity requirements.

**Details**

This is an exempt, salaried, full-time position on our Consumable Manufacturing team.

Join us! We're excited for what you can bring to our team. Here are a few things we provide to make sure you have a great experience. Learn more about our team by visiting our website.

**Benefits**

* Health insurance
* 401k Matching
* Paid Time Off
* The opportunity to make a global impact

To fulfill our mission and build world-changing technology, we've put together a diverse, multi-disciplinary top-notch team, a culture of innovation, learning, adaptability, and excellence and environment where people love coming to work.

We value diversity on our teams. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, status as a qualified individual with disability, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

jobs.title: Phlebotomist-Lab Technician
jobs.description:
HJ Staffing is currently seeking one (1) dedicated **Lab Technician / Qualified Phlebotomist** to support the Laboratory Department at Austin State Hospital.

In this role, you will play a vital part in patient care by performing blood draws and laboratory support duties for individuals receiving inpatient habilitation or rehabilitation services. We are looking for a compassionate, reliable professional experienced in working within a psychiatric or specialized care facility setting.

**Location:** Austin State Hospital – 4110 Guadalupe St, Austin, TX 78751

**Department:** Lab Department

**Position Type:** Full-Time / Contract (3 to 6 Months, with potential extension)

**Schedule:** 7:00 AM – 1:00 PM (Part-Time / Standard Shift Hours)

### **Key Responsibilities**

* Perform phlebotomy (blood draws) and standard laboratory technician duties in accordance with the Rules and Regulations relating to Lab Technicians in the State of Texas.
* Work compassionately and effectively with individuals with mental illness, intellectual/developmental disabilities, chemical dependency, and social or physical disorders.
* Adhere strictly to the rules, regulations, and policies of HHSC, Austin State Hospital, and HJ Staffing (including leave and attendance policies).
* Complete all mandatory daily reporting, laboratory documentation, and administrative duties as assigned.

### **Schedule & Hours**

* **Standard Shift:** 7:00 AM – 1:00 PM
* **Training Requirement:** Must be available for 2 non-consecutive days of full-day training (Day 1 and Day 6) from **8:00 AM to 5:00 PM**. Remaining training will take place during normal work schedule hours.
* **Overtime Policy:** Overtime (>40 hours/week) is generally not permitted unless explicitly pre-approved and scheduled on an individual basis by Austin State Hospital.

### **Qualifications & Requirements**

* **Experience:** One (1) year of phlebotomy / blood-drawing experience is preferred.
* **Licensure & Certifications:** Must hold and maintain current, active state/national phlebotomy or lab technician certifications throughout the duration of the assignment.
* **Professionalism:** Strong communication skills, reliability, and the ability to maintain composure in a mental health care facility setting.

### **Clearance & Onboarding Requirements**

*Official start dates are dependent upon candidate clearance.* Prior to beginning services at the facility, selected candidates must successfully complete and pass all required clearance requirements, including but not limited to:

* Facility Background Check
* Complete Immunization Documentation & Medical Clearance
* COVID-19 Testing Clearance
* Completion of initial Facility Orientation/Training (held Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM – 5:00 PM)

jobs.title: Quality Assurance Technician
jobs.description:
**Essential Functions**

A Ziegenfelder Quality Technician is responsible for:

* Ensuring that finished Ziegenfelder treats are ready for packaging by properly preparing raw material inputs, monitoring production processes, and inspecting final products to ensure customer satisfaction.
* Reviewing and documenting quality assurance processes and making recommendations for improvements.
* Manipulate a variety of stainless-steel hard pipes and flexible hosing to perform CIPs and batch processing.
* Participate in plant sanitation activities including floor scrubbing, drain cleaning, and other manual sanitation tasks.
* Participate in environmental monitoring program by collecting samples of finished product, work in progress, on equipment and around facility.
* Review and record microbiological data and report concerns and findings to Quality Manager.
* Use HMI to appropriately call ingredients for bulk processing and transfer of batches.
* Conducting production support to include mix making, equipment cleaning, product quality testing/sampling, and completion of the master sanitation schedule tasks.
* Verifying finished product meets quality standards of color, taste, quantity, wrap, and Rainbow Array.
* Adhering to HACCP, GMP, SOP, and SSOP programs and coordinating all documentation to ensure compliance with all federal, state, local, and Ziegenfelder directives, policies, and procedures.
* Perform chemistry testing to ensure product specifications.
* Troubleshoot equipment malfunctions and work cross-functionally with Production and Maintenance departments.
* Perform multiple quality checks and records results in the data control system as well as document batch records.
* Complete internal lab functions including environmental sampling and document completion.
* Conducting regular audits of documentation to ensure compliance with applicable federal, state, local, and Ziegenfelder directives, policies, and procedures.

Qualifications and Education Requirements

* One plus years within a food manufacturing facility, preferred.
* Preference will be given to Food Science, Food Technology Degree, or other related fields, however not required, experience will be considered.
* Experience and training with Food Safety, HACCP, SQF, Sanitation (SSOP & GMP) and/or other food safety systems and Quality Assurance process improvement skills required. SQF certification preferred but not required.
* Strong computer skills to include the use of Microsoft Office products.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

**Physical Abilities**

* Standing up to 12 hours per day.
* Moving and lifting objects weighing up to 50 lbs. regularly, daily.
* Bending, twisting, reaching and grasping actions.
* Good spatial awareness working around manufacturing equipment.

**Working Conditions**

* Subject to cold temperatures of less than 32F for more than one hour with proper protection equipment.
* May be subject to noise above 85 decibels with proper protection equipment

**Compensation & Benefits**

* **Starting Pay:** $18.75/hour
* **Schedule:** 40 hours per week with set days off
* **Benefits:** Begin on the first day after 60 days of employment
* **401(k) with company matching**
* **Employee discounts**
* **Paid holidays**

**Who We Are**

The Ziegenfelder Company is part of the **Armstrong Group**, a family-owned organization founded in 1946. With over 2,400 employees nationwide, our brands span multiple industries including utilities, protection services, development, and frozen novelties.

At Ziegenfelder, we specialize in producing high-quality frozen twin pops under the **Budget Saver** brand, as well as private label products for major retailers like Walmart, Kroger, and Dollar General. Our facilities are located in Wheeling, WV; Chino, CA; Denver, CO; and Lockhart, TX.

We value **integrity, creativity, and innovation**, and are committed to positively impacting our workforce and the communities we serve.

**Armstrong is an Equal Opportunity Employer.**

**Who We Are**  
The Armstrong Group is a family owned and operated collection of diverse companies. What began in 1946 as Armstrong County Line Construction, founded by Jud L. Sedwick in Kittanning, PA, has now grown into an organization that encompasses multiple industries and employs over 2,400 individuals nationwide. Our brands include Armstrong Utilities, Guardian Protection, Armstrong Development, 4Front Solutions, Twin Pops, and Armstrong Comfort Solutions.
  
  
Armstrong is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

**Brief Job Description:**

Under general supervision of the Endocrine (Endos) Screening Group Manager uses considerable knowledge to independently perform highly complex immunofluorometric testing including Immunoreactive trypsinogen (IRT), 17-hydroxyprogesterone (17-OHP), thyroxine (T4), and thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH), and galactose 1-phospate uridyl transferace (GALT) analysis on high volume neonatal screening specimens. Serves as an authority on test procedures in the EIA laboratory. Utilizes considerable working knowledge of all procedures to participate in maintaining analytic accuracy. Responsible for independently performing specimen preparation and analysis, quality control and assay acceptability, data and work list evaluation, result entry, release of final results, maintenance and troubleshooting of equipment, and training of personnel. Responsible for making significant decisions on the accuracy of laboratory tests on human specimens. Independently determines and releases complex results based on Standard Operating Protocols (SOP). Actively participates in the safety program. Supervisor will assign a small portion of daily work providing general instruction for routine tasks and detailed instructions for non-routine tasks. Duties are independently performed with considerable latitude, adherence to standard protocol and with use of scientific knowledge and independent judgment.

Work hours/days and laboratory assignments may vary; all staff members will be required to work on Saturday and some holidays as part of a rotating schedule.

Recognizes delays in completion of specimen testing, result reporting, and other essential functions and notifies the supervisor immediately. Identifies problems with atypical test results, consulting with upper-level personnel. Recognizes delays in completion of specimen testing, result reporting, and other essential functions and notifies the supervisor immediately. (25%)
